title: POC success signoff and benchmark reporting format - Caspian Health
next_steps: Redwood to share go/no-go spreadsheet with thresholds and reporting template by 2025-10-10
Priya to provide benchmark config (instance types, batch sizes, quant) and runbook by 2025-10-12
Caspian to upload 3 canonical workloads and sample golden outputs by 2025-10-09
Schedule live benchmark kickoff (1.5 hr) week of 2025-10-13
action_items: Ethan Rivera: Share detailed pricing, SLA language, and go/no-go spreadsheet (due 2025-10-10)
Priya Shah: Build and validate benchmark harness; push images to customer registry and share runbook (due 2025-10-12)
Lena Ortiz: Deliver three workload manifests + expected pass/fail labels (due 2025-10-09)
Markus Jensen: Provision VPN and S3 endpoint, test ingress (due 2025-10-11)
summary: Short call to finalize the POC success criteria and agree on the format of the benchmark report. Primary goals: lock go/no-go thresholds for latency, throughput and quality; confirm sample workloads; agree on reporting CSV and human-eval pass criteria; align on timeline for benchmark runs and access requirements.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Ethan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:00:07] Lena (Caspian): Lena here.
[00:00:09] Markus (Caspian): Markus on infra.
[00:00:11] Sana (Caspian): Sana for product.
[00:00:13] Oliver (Caspian): Oliver, data ops.
[00:00:15] Priya (Redwood SE): Priya here.
[00:00:18] Anika (Redwood CSM): And Anika.
[00:00:20] Ethan: Cool. Objective for the 45-ish minute call: finalize go/no-go thresholds and the reporting format so both teams can run predictable benchmarks. We'll walk the thresholds, discuss workload sizing, and agree next steps.
[00:00:34] Lena: Sounds good. We're mainly worried about two things: p95 latency for our interactive triage UI and overall cost per 1k tokens.
[00:00:42] Ethan: Totally. Priya, do you want to run through the proposed thresholds we sent earlier?
[00:00:46] Priya: Yep. I have the sheet open. For the interactive workflows (median 120 tokens, 95th percentile target) we propose p95 <= 250 ms for hosted and <= 200 ms on Dedicated with autoscaling. For batch scoring workflows (avg 1k tokens) target end-to-end latency per request <= 3s and throughput >= 150 req/min sustained.
[00:01:09] Markus: Those p95 numbers seem aggressive for 1k token completions, can you clarify tokenization? Are you including generation + network + post-processing?
[00:01:18] Priya: Good question. Our definition in the spreadsheet is end-to-end server-side generation time (from request receive to last token emitted) plus middleware overhead measured inside the VPC. Network time is recorded separately in the report as a column — we want server-side p95 <= X.
[00:01:34] Sana: And on quality, what are we using? We sent a prompt set last week but we need a clear pass/fail rubric.
[00:01:40] Ethan: We're proposing a two-pronged quality check: automated metrics and human eval. Automated: for classification/regression tasks we'll use accuracy/F1 with thresholds per workload (we'll put exact numbers in the sheet). For free-form generation we want a human-rated pass rate >= 90% on a 3-rater majority scheme comparing Redwood output vs baseline. That is go.
[00:01:59] Lena: 90% seems high; our baselines are tuned models. Could we allow a delta margin, like no more than 3% absolute drop from baseline?
[00:02:06] Priya: Yes, we can specify relative delta. For free-form, primary metric is human pass rate >= 90% OR within 3% absolute of your baseline human pass on the same prompts. We'll include both columns in the report.
[00:02:18] Oliver: For these human evals, can Redwood provide an evaluation UI or do we run it?
[00:02:22] Anika: We can provide a lightweight human-eval rubric and an exportable CSV with rows for prompt id, Redwood output, baseline output, rater, score. We can also host a secure ephemeral UI if you prefer.
[00:02:34] Markus: Security: we need SOC 2 details and KMS integration. Also, on the Private/Dedicated split, some datasets can't leave our VPC.
[00:02:42] Ethan: Understood. For this POC we agreed earlier on a Private deployment with a customer-managed VPC. We'll record whether the benchmark run was in Private mode. For KMS we support customer-managed keys; we'll need an IAM/KMS contact.
[00:02:55] Markus: I'll assign that after the call.
[00:02:58] Sana: On workload sizing, we prepared three canonical workloads: interactive triage (short prompts), batch clinical note summarization (longer), and reranking for search. Size-wise, what are you expecting in terms of sample counts for statistical significance?
[00:03:13] Priya: Good point. We recommend at minimum 1k samples for interactive-type tests, 300 samples for long-form summarization (due to reviewer cost), and at least 500 queries for reranking. The report will include sample size, confidence intervals for key metrics, and p-values where relevant.
[00:03:31] Lena: Can you explain how you'll compute cost-per-1k tokens? We need that to evaluate unit economics.
[00:03:35] Priya: We compute total compute spend for the run (broken down by GPU-hours and instance types) divided by total tokens processed, normalized to 1k tokens. We'll show token breakdowns (prompt vs completion), and also amortized cost for caching/batching.
[00:03:49] Oliver: Do you simulate caching effects? Some requests have high prefix reuse in our product.
[00:03:53] Priya: Yes, the harness can replay sequential traffic to exercise KV cache and prefix caching. We will run two variants: cold-cache and warm-cache (with a warmup period) and report both.
[00:04:03] Markus: For the throughput tests, what concurrency model will you use?
[00:04:07] Priya: We'll use a closed-loop client model that ramps to target QPS and measures latency distributions under sustained load. We'll share the JMeter/locust scenario in the runbook.
[00:04:16] Sana: On reporting, we need a single-page executive summary plus a detailed CSV and a short runbook. What's your CSV schema?
[00:04:22] Ethan: Our standard CSV includes: run_id, workload_name, sample_id, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, server_side_latency_ms, network_latency_ms, gpu_instance, batch_size, quantization_flag, model_variant, pass_human_eval (Y/N), automated_score, comment. We'll attach the go/no-go flags at the top with a short rationale.
[00:04:40] Lena: Can you also include confidence intervals for p95?
[00:04:43] Priya: We will include bootstrapped confidence intervals for percentiles and append a histogram for latency.
[00:04:49] Markus: Nice. On model variants, we intend to test both unquantized and int8-quantized variants. How does Redwood handle functionally equivalent fallbacks during the run?
[00:04:59] Priya: The harness will pin a model variant per run. If you want automatic fallback tests, we can do a separate degrade test where we intentionally pull capacity and test fallback to a cheaper variant, then report functional parity differences.
[00:05:12] Sana: Let's reserve fallback tests for later; first focus on baseline parity.
[00:05:15] Ethan: Agree. Now the go/no-go thresholds in plain language: 1) Latency: server-side p95 <= 250 ms for interactive; 2) Throughput: batch >= 150 req/min for 1k token jobs; 3) Quality: human pass rate >= 90% or within 3% absolute of baseline; 4) Cost: cost per 1k tokens must be <= 0.30 USD (example — we'll lock final $ in sheet). If any of the first three fail, that's a no-go; cost failure is a partial fail and can be considered if other metrics exceed expectations.
[00:05:48] Lena: Cost target needs to be tuned — 0.30 could be optimistic. Can we put ranges? Like target <= 0.30, acceptable <= 0.45?
[00:05:56] Ethan: Yep, we'll put green/amber/red thresholds in the sheet. Go = green, conditional = amber (requires mitigation plan), fail = red.
[00:06:04] Oliver: For the final report, can you include an appendix of raw logs and model seeding so our auditors can reproduce results?
[00:06:11] Priya: We'll include a reproducibility section with model seeds, command lines, and container digests. Raw logs will be available in an S3 bucket you control for privacy.
[00:06:20] Markus: Great. About timeline: when do you expect to run the live benchmark?
[00:06:24] Ethan: If we get access and workloads by 2025-10-09, Priya's team can run first pass 10/13-10/15 with a live kickoff 10/14. Results draft on 10/17 and final report 10/21. Is that workable?
[00:06:35] Lena: That works for product, though we'll need Markus to confirm infra by 10/11.
[00:06:40] Markus: I'll confirm.
[00:06:43] Sana: A few nitty-gritty items: labeling for human eval (3 raters, blind), and we want an export with rater IDs obfuscated.
[00:06:50] Anika: Understood — we'll anonymize rater IDs and provide the CSV with just scores.
[00:06:55] Ethan: Anything else on acceptance criteria?
[00:06:58] Lena: Can we add an SLA clause for POC runs — that Redwood will maintain a target uptime for the dedicated cluster during the test window? We need minimal interference.
[00:07:07] Ethan: We can commit to a 99% availability during the scheduled benchmark window for Dedicated runs, and we'll document it in the runbook.
[00:07:14] Markus: On the subject of compliance, we need an export of audit logs for every request in the run. Can Redwood produce that?
[00:07:20] Priya: Yes, request-level audit logs (request id, timestamp, model, tokens) can be exported to your S3. We'll include a sample structure.
[00:07:27] Oliver: One more technical: how do you measure prompt vs completion tokens? Tokenizers differ.
[00:07:32] Priya: We'll use the same tokenizer library as the model runtime (we'll record library version) and include token counts as measured server-side. If you want to normalize against your tokenizer we can include a cross-walk.
[00:07:42] Lena: Ok. Any objections to the report template?
[00:07:45] Sana: No objections. Just want clarity on human eval cost and who pays for raters.
[00:07:50] Ethan: Typically the vendor covers a baseline human-eval for the initial POC; if you need larger-scale labeling we can discuss cost-sharing. We'll note that in next steps.
[00:07:58] Lena: Fine.
[00:08:00] Ethan: Quick recap of next steps: (1) Caspian shares three workload manifests + golden outputs by 10/09; (2) Redwood shares finalized go/no-go spreadsheet + report template by 10/10; (3) infra access (VPN/S3) provisioned by 10/11; (4) kickoff 10/14 and run 10/13-10/15; (5) draft report 10/17, final 10/21.
[00:08:20] Priya: I'll ping the repo with the harness and a sample locust/jmeter scenario.
[00:08:24] Markus: I'll open the ticket for VPN/KMS.
[00:08:27] Lena: We'll review the spreadsheet and reply with any changes on 10/10.
[00:08:31] Ethan: Perfect. End of call — thanks everyone.
[00:08:35] Sana: Thanks.
[00:08:36] Anika: Thanks all, follow up in email.
[00:08:38] [END OF RECORDING]
